newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Supply squeeze seen pushing up prices.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Supply squeeze seen pushing up prices.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to move higher this week due to continuing concerns over low copra supply from the Philippines, vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
Increasing demand of the commodity in the local market is also seen pushing up prices overseas, they said.

"I see this market moving in a narrow trading range as copra turnover remains slow and negative crushing margins continue to prevail among millers. As a consequence, selling pressure would be limited," said a senior trader in one of the Philippine's largest coconut oil millers.
Another trader said he expected the market to go up between $10 and $20 per tonne this week.
A third trader, however, said he expected prices to be steady because of the prevailing thin market overseas.
The trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines Inc (UCAP) said the average done deals on coconut oil in Europe increased to $777 per tonne CIF last week from the previous $766.25.

A senior trader with a Philippine coconut miller estimated coconut oil exports in both Europe and the United States this month to reach 94,000 tonnes, of which 30,000 tonnes are carry over stocks from December.
"The 30,000 tonnes included in the January export data were late deliveries from December due to ship delays," the trader said.
Philippine coconut oil export from January 1 to 22 this year reached 59,060 tonnes, UCAP said.
Exports in January 1996 had reached 74,074 tonnes, it added.

Some 16,000 tonnes in fresh coconut oil stocks on board the MV Auriga are expected to arrive in Rotterdam on January 31. Another ship, MV Blue Sapphire, with a cargo of 20,000 tonnes was scheduled to arrive in Rotterdam between January 15 and 30.
Stocks in Rotterdam and the United States this week will depend on the arrival of fresh stocks, traders said.
Coconut stocks in Rotterdam as of January 20 reached 20,732 tonnes while stocks in the United States cannot be imemdiately determined, they said.
Monthly coconut oil requirement in Rotterdam was placed between 45,000 and 55,000 tonnes and between 40,000 and 45,000 tonnes in the United States.
